instruction: Access the receipt image OIP.jpg in /home/user, convert it to PNG, and save it to the desktop as 'receipt.png'.

metadata.explanation: Task requires opening the receipt JPEG image and converting it to PNG format, saving on the desktop. The custom getter extracts image properties (format, dimensions) using PIL. The metric checks: 1) File format is PNG, 2) Width >= 100 pixels, 3) Height >= 100 pixels. This gives partial credit: format check (33%), width check (33%), height check (33%). The dimensions are reasonable minimums since the original receipt image is larger.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic is correct: extracts image properties (format, width, height) from the target file path using PIL
Metric logic is correct: properly handles expected parameter when type='rule' by directly accessing expected['format'], expected['min_width'], expected['min_height']
Complete coverage: evaluator verifies file exists at desktop path, format is PNG (conversion successful), and has reasonable dimensions
Expected values are semantically correct: format='PNG' verifies JPEG-to-PNG conversion, min dimensions (100x100) are reasonable sanity checks
Data flow is correct: getter extracts properties -> metric compares format and dimensions -> partial credit scoring (3 checks, each 33%)
Static validation warning about 'dict vs Dict' is a false positive - the parameter handling is actually correct
